events.title: Georgian Dream Declared Winner of Disputed Parliamentary Election
events.detail: The Central Election Commission declared Georgian Dream the winner with nearly 54% of the vote. OSCE/ODIHR observers and independent monitors reported a large-scale, multi-faceted rigging scheme including voter intimidation, vote-buying, compromised ballot secrecy and multiple voting. President Salome Zourabichvili and the opposition refused to recognize the result, alleging massive fraud and Russian interference.

events.title: Prosecutors Open 47 Election-Fraud Cases, Arrest Two Over Ballot Stuffing in Marneuli
events.detail: Georgia's Prosecutor's Office opened an investigation into election fraud allegations and arrested two people accused of stuffing ballot boxes in Marneuli during the October 26 vote, part of 47 fraud cases opened nationally.

events.title: PM Kobakhidze Announces Suspension of EU Accession Talks Until 2028
events.detail: Prime Minister Irakli Kobakhidze announced Georgia would not initiate EU accession negotiations until 2028 and would refuse EU budget support in the meantime. Legal experts and 200 National Bank of Georgia employees called the move unconstitutional, citing Article 78 of the constitution, which mandates EU/NATO integration. Roughly 80% of Georgians support EU membership according to polling.

events.title: Riot Police Use Water Cannon and Alleged Chemical Agents on Rustaveli Avenue
events.detail: Within hours of Kobakhidze's announcement, thousands marched on Parliament and blocked Rustaveli Avenue in Tbilisi, with parallel protests in Kutaisi, Batumi, Gori and Zugdidi. Special forces dispersed the crowd overnight using water cannon; protesters reported chemical burns on skin and eyes, suggesting additives in the water.

events.title: Parliament's Electoral College Elects Mikheil Kavelashvili President
events.detail: A 225-member electoral college controlled by Georgian Dream elected former footballer and MP Mikheil Kavelashvili president, with 224 of 225 votes. The opposition boycotted the vote. Incumbent president Salome Zourabichvili called the process illegitimate and said she would not leave office.

events.title: Public Defender Documents Ill-Treatment of 225 of 327 Detainees
events.detail: Georgia's Public Defender (Ombudsman) reported visiting 327 people detained during post-election protests; 225 alleged ill-treatment and 157 showed visible injuries. Transparency International Georgia and other rights groups said the evidence pointed to systemic, planned torture of peaceful demonstrators.

events.title: United States Sanctions Bidzina Ivanishvili
events.detail: The US State Department sanctioned Georgian Dream founder Bidzina Ivanishvili, saying he and his party had undermined democratic institutions and 'derailed Georgia's Euro-Atlantic future' for Russia's benefit. The EU has been unable to impose equivalent sanctions due to vetoes from Hungary and Slovakia, which require unanimity among member states.

events.title: 49 Interior Ministry Staff Resign, Including All 16 Water-Cannon Operators
events.detail: Between December 25 and 29, 49 Ministry of Internal Affairs employees resigned over their role in dispersing protests, including the head of protest-dispersal operations and all 16 water-cannon operators. Former official Irakli Shaishmelashvili later said the violence had been carried out 'under orders' from ministry leadership.

events.title: Kavelashvili Inaugurated; Zourabichvili Calls It 'a Mockery of Democracy'
events.detail: Mikheil Kavelashvili was inaugurated as president and Salome Zourabichvili departed the Orbeliani presidential palace, denouncing the inauguration as 'a mockery of democracy' while maintaining that she remained Georgia's legitimate head of state.

events.title: Journalist Mzia Amaglobeli Arrested in Batumi
events.detail: Netgazeti and Batumelebi founder Mzia Amaglobeli was arrested outside Batumi police headquarters after allegedly slapping police chief Irakli Dgebuadze, whom she says spat in her face and insulted her during a pro-European protest. Her case became the emblem of Georgia's press-freedom crackdown.

events.title: Saakashvili Sentenced to 9 More Years on Embezzlement Charges
events.detail: A Tbilisi court sentenced imprisoned former president Mikheil Saakashvili to nine additional years for alleged embezzlement, on top of earlier convictions. His supporters call the prosecutions politically motivated; he has staged repeated hunger strikes and is held under restrictive conditions in a civilian hospital.

events.title: Saakashvili's Combined Sentence Extended to 12.5 Years
events.detail: A further 4.5-year sentence for illegal re-entry into Georgia brought Saakashvili's cumulative prison term to roughly 12.5 years, extending his imprisonment through much of the next decade.

events.title: Parliament Passes Foreign Agents Registration Act
events.detail: Parliament passed the Foreign Agents Registration Act in its third reading; the President signed it April 2 and it entered into force June 1, 2025. NGO and media directors who fail to register as acting on behalf of a 'foreign principal' face criminal prosecution and up to five years in prison. It builds on the 2024 'Transparency of Foreign Influence' law requiring groups with over 20% foreign funding to register as serving foreign interests.

events.title: Broadcasting Law Bans Foreign Funding of Media Outlets
events.detail: The Georgian Dream-controlled parliament approved a Broadcasting Law banning foreign funding of media. Violators face fines, 300–500 hours of community service or up to six years in prison; regulators can seize prohibited foreign funds and demand banking records from broadcasters and sponsors.

events.title: Independent Media Say They Are Running Out of 'Ways to Survive'
events.detail: CPJ reported independent Georgian outlets losing viable funding models as the new foreign-funding laws close off grants and foreign advertising revenue that had sustained investigative and opposition-aligned media.

events.title: Russia Resumes Direct Moscow–Tbilisi Flights, Lifts Visa Requirement
events.detail: Vladimir Putin signed decrees canceling visa requirements for Georgian citizens and lifting Russia's 2019 ban on direct flights; Russian carriers began operating seven flights weekly between Moscow and Tbilisi, deepening informal Russia-Georgia normalization even as EU ties froze.

events.title: Four Opposition Figures Jailed for Boycotting Parliamentary Commission
events.detail: Giorgi Vashadze, Zurab Japaridze, Mamuka Khazaradze and Badri Japaridze were sentenced to seven-to-eight months in prison and barred from public office for two years after refusing to appear before a Georgian Dream-created parliamentary commission investigating the pre-2012 Saakashvili era. Amnesty International called it a deepening crackdown on government critics.

events.title: European Parliament Demands Amaglobeli's Release
events.detail: The European Parliament passed a resolution demanding Mzia Amaglobeli's immediate release and denouncing what it called systematic attacks on independent media by the Georgian government, part of a series of five EU Parliament resolutions on Georgia since December 2024.

events.title: Opposition Leader Nika Gvaramia Jailed
events.detail: Coalition for Change leader Nika Gvaramia was sentenced to eight months in prison and barred from holding office for two years over his refusal to cooperate with the Saakashvili-era parliamentary commission, joining fellow opposition leaders Nika Melia and Irakli Okruashvili in detention on similar charges.

events.title: Amaglobeli Sentenced to Two Years in Prison
events.detail: Batumi City Court judge Nino Sakhelashvili sentenced Mzia Amaglobeli to two years in prison for resisting or using violence against a police officer, after the initial, more serious assault charge was reduced. CPJ and press-freedom groups worldwide called the verdict 'outrageous' and politically motivated.

era: October Elections, Uprising Attempt & Party Bans (Oct–Dec 2025)

events.title: Amaglobeli and Poczobut Named 2025 Sakharov Prize Laureates
events.detail: The European Parliament named jailed Georgian journalist Mzia Amaglobeli and Belarusian journalist Andrzej Poczobut co-recipients of the 2025 Sakharov Prize for Freedom of Thought, its highest human-rights honor, spotlighting her imprisonment internationally.

events.title: Georgian Dream Sweeps Municipal Elections Amid Opposition Boycott
events.detail: Eight pro-European opposition parties boycotted the October 4 local elections, calling participation illegitimate. Georgian Dream won all 64 municipalities, taking 70–90% of the vote in many; turnout fell to 41%, ten points below 2021. Critics said the boycott handed the ruling party an uncontested mandate to tighten control.

events.title: Protesters Attempt to Storm Presidential Palace; Organizers Arrested
events.detail: Tens of thousands rallied on Rustaveli Avenue and Freedom Square behind opera singer Paata Burchuladze's call for a 'peaceful revolution' and transfer of power from Bidzina Ivanishvili. That evening a crowd tried to storm Orbeliani presidential palace; riot police used water cannon, pepper spray and tear gas. Georgia's health ministry reported 21 security personnel and 6 protesters injured. Burchuladze and other organizers were arrested and charged with attempting to overthrow the government, facing up to nine years in prison.
events.confidenceReason: Government and opposition dispute whether the storming attempt was organized insurrection or a spontaneous escalation of a peaceful march.

events.title: Parliament Passes Law Enabling Bans on Opposition Parties
events.detail: The one-party parliament adopted a legislative package empowering the state to seek court-ordered bans on political parties and indefinite deprivation of political rights for their members, citing the October 4 unrest as justification. Legal scholars called the package unconstitutional.

events.title: Georgian Dream Files Lawsuit to Ban Three Main Opposition Parties
events.detail: The ruling party petitioned the Constitutional Court to ban the United National Movement, Ahali (Coalition for Change) and Lelo for Georgia under Article 23 of the constitution, alleging they sought to overthrow constitutional order. Georgian Dream said it might also pursue bans against smaller parties including Droa, Girchi – More Freedom, Strategy Aghmashenebeli, European Georgia, the Federalists and the Republicans. Parliament's speaker said a ruling could come by mid-2026.

events.title: Kutaisi Court of Appeal Upholds Amaglobeli's Two-Year Sentence
events.detail: The Kutaisi Court of Appeal rejected Mzia Amaglobeli's appeal and upheld her two-year sentence. The European Federation of Journalists condemned the ruling as confirming a politically motivated verdict against a Sakharov Prize laureate.

events.title: Amaglobeli Awarded Sakharov Prize in Strasbourg (in Absentia)
events.detail: The European Parliament formally awarded the 2025 Sakharov Prize to Mzia Amaglobeli, represented by fellow journalist Irma Dimitradze. Her prepared remarks said the regime 'destroys free journalism, abolishes opposition political parties and imprisons their leaders... yet it has failed to silence the protests,' and appealed: 'Fight with us and for us.'

events.title: New Law Bans Sidewalk Protests, Escalating to Criminal Penalties
events.detail: Parliament passed a law prohibiting protests on sidewalks with escalating administrative and eventually criminal sanctions for repeat violations. Legal scholars characterized the measure, part of a wave of over twenty repressive laws passed since late 2024, as unconstitutional.

events.title: European Commission Publishes 8th Visa-Suspension Mechanism Report on Georgia
events.detail: The European Commission's eighth report under the visa-suspension mechanism documented Georgia's continued failure to meet fundamental-rights benchmarks tied to visa-free travel, setting the stage for a formal suspension in March 2026.

events.title: CPJ Report Finds Georgia Violated Amaglobeli's Right to a Fair Trial
events.detail: The Committee to Protect Journalists published an in-depth report concluding Georgian courts violated Mzia Amaglobeli's right to a fair trial, citing due-process failures in both the original verdict and the appeal.

events.title: Amnesty Warns of New Bill Criminalizing Foreign-Funded Civic Activity
events.detail: Amnesty International warned that a new Georgian Dream bill would further criminalize foreign funding for civic activity, tightening the vise on the NGOs and media groups that survived the 2025 foreign-agents and broadcasting laws.

events.title: Georgia's Supreme Court Declines to Hear Amaglobeli's Final Appeal
events.detail: Georgia's Supreme Court declined to consider Mzia Amaglobeli's appeal of her two-year sentence, exhausting her domestic legal options and leaving international bodies as her remaining avenue for redress.

events.title: EU Suspends Visa-Free Travel for Georgian Diplomatic Passport Holders
events.detail: The European Commission suspended visa-free Schengen travel for holders of Georgian diplomatic, service and official passports for 12 months, citing 'deliberate and persisting violations' of democratic commitments. The Commission separately warned Georgia's entire population risks losing visa-free travel if backsliding continues.

events.title: Opposition Groups Sign Joint Declaration Ahead of Party-Ban Ruling
events.detail: Facing the pending Constitutional Court case against the United National Movement, Ahali and Lelo for Georgia, opposition parties signed a joint declaration coordinating their response, prompting Georgian Dream to amend and expand its lawsuit to include the Federalists party.

events.title: Thousands Rally in Tbilisi for Independence Day Pro-EU Protest
events.detail: Thousands of demonstrators marked Georgia's Independence Day with a pro-EU rally in Tbilisi, combining national-holiday commemoration with the now 18-month-old protest movement's core demands: release of political prisoners and resumption of EU accession talks.

events.title: Amnesty International: Georgia Built a 'Coordinated System' to Crush Dissent
events.detail: Amnesty International's report 'Anatomy of Repression: Georgia, 500 Days of Protest, Crackdown and Resilience' concluded Georgia is undergoing 'one of the most serious erosions of human rights since independence,' documenting how the government weaponized disinformation, fast-tracked repressive laws through its parliamentary majority, and instrumentalized courts and police against opponents. Ombudsman data showed 78–88% of protesters detained in 2024–2025 reported ill-treatment.

events.title: HRW: New Laws 'Devastate' Independent Civic Groups
events.detail: Human Rights Watch reported that the cumulative effect of Georgia's foreign-agents, broadcasting and grant-restriction laws had devastated independent civil society, forcing closures and mass staff departures at NGOs that had operated for decades.

events.title: Georgia Excluded From 2026 NATO Summit Partner List
events.detail: Georgia was absent from the 2026 NATO summit's official programme and side forums for the first time as a longstanding partner nation. NATO had already suspended 5 of 17 cooperation initiatives under the NATO-Georgia Substantial Package over the foreign-influence laws and political polarization.

events.title: Transparency International Georgia Lists 91 Political Prisoners
events.detail: Transparency International Georgia published an updated list of 91 people meeting PACE Resolution 1900 (2012) criteria for political prisoners, including protesters, opposition politicians and former Ivanishvili business associates. TI-Georgia's Sandro Baramidze said the true number had been higher before some detainees accepted prosecutorial plea deals.
events.confidenceReason: Georgian Dream disputes the classification and does not recognize any of the 91 as political prisoners.

events.title: 34th Saturday March Marks 623rd Consecutive Day of Protest
events.detail: Tbilisi's pro-European movement held its 34th Saturday mass march, with the 623rd consecutive day of daily demonstrations at Parliament and the Tbilisi City Council. Core demands remained unchanged: release of political prisoners, abolition of repressive laws, and resumption of the EU accession path.

events.title: Protesters Highlight Mass Emigration Under Georgian Dream Rule
events.detail: A Tbilisi march themed 'When the state serves an oligarch, people leave' spotlighted emigration data showing more than 400,000 Georgian citizens have left the country since Georgian Dream took power in 2012, out of a population under 4 million.

events.title: Adjara TV Journalist Detained After Reporting Repeated Attacks
events.detail: Adjara TV host Koba Partenadze, who had reported being physically attacked and threatened with a knife in Batumi over several days (including a homophobic-slur assault on Aug 9-10 that led to two arrests), was himself detained on Aug 17 while being questioned as a witness. Police charged him with petty hooliganism and disobeying a police officer; the Batumi City Court fined him 2,000 GEL. The Charter of Journalistic Ethics called for urgent protection of Partenadze rather than his prosecution.

media.caption: Adjara TV journalist Koba Partenadze, detained Aug 17 after reporting repeated attacks in Batumi

events.confidenceReason: Confirmed by Interior Ministry statement, Batumi City Court fine, and multiple Georgian outlets.

events.title: Georgian Citizen Released After Illegal Detention Near Tskhinvali Occupation Line
events.detail: Lasha Gulitashvili was detained by South Ossetian border guards on Aug 17 near Perevi village, Sachkhere municipality, close to the Tskhinvali occupation line, and accused by Tskhinvali's Res news agency of illegally crossing the boundary. Georgia's State Security Service said it used its EUMM-operated hotline and other channels to secure his release by Aug 19, noting 34 similar illegal-detention cases were recorded around the occupation line in 2025.

media.caption: Bershueti village, Gori municipality, near the Tskhinvali occupation line
media.source: Democracy Research Institute via Civil Georgia

events.confidenceReason: Confirmed by Georgia's State Security Service statement and independent reporting.

events.title: PM Kobakhidze Defends 1783 Treaty of Georgievsk With Russia
events.detail: Prime Minister Irakli Kobakhidze held a briefing defending King Erekle II's 1783 decision to place eastern Georgia under Russian protection via the Treaty of Georgievsk, calling it 'the only correct and unavoidable decision' and arguing Georgia 'survived as a nation' through the accord, despite Russia's subsequent failure to honor it and its 1801 annexation of the kingdom. He dismissed critics of the framing as 'pseudo-liberals,' drawing parallels to what he called Western pressure on Georgia today.

media.caption: PM Irakli Kobakhidze at an Aug 18 briefing defending the 1783 Treaty of Georgievsk

events.confidenceReason: Direct on-record briefing reported by Civil Georgia.

events.title: Jailed Ex-PM Garibashvili Accuses Georgian Dream of 'Setting a Trap'
events.detail: Imprisoned former two-time Prime Minister Irakli Garibashvili, serving a five-year sentence from a January 2026 money-laundering plea deal, began a series of Facebook statements on Aug 17 alleging he was pressured to plead guilty to a new corruption charge on Ivanishvili's instructions to permanently end his political career. By Aug 20 he said the government 'set me up with a dirty provocation, laid an unmanly trap,' and claimed officials threatened to arrest his 75-year-old father. He said he had stayed silent out of 'absolute loyalty' to Ivanishvili but was now forced to 'fight.' PM Kobakhidze dismissed the claims as 'problematic,' noting Garibashvili had already admitted guilt. It is the first public break with Ivanishvili by a former close ally.

media.caption: Former PM Irakli Garibashvili, who has accused Georgian Dream of pressuring him from prison

events.confidenceReason: Garibashvili's allegations are unverified beyond his own statements and a letter he published; the government disputes his account.

events.title: Russian MFA's Zakharova Demands Probe of 'Anti-Russian Manifestations' in Georgia
events.detail: Russian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Maria Zakharova told a briefing that 'anti-Russian manifestations' against Russian nationals in Georgia 'must be thoroughly investigated, and those responsible must be held accountable,' citing unspecified 'serious incidents' including a July altercation in Kakheti. Georgian Dream leadership has separately blamed a 'deep state' for fueling 'Russophobia' to damage Russian tourism, which has risen 1.6x since 2023, while Georgia's State Security Service opened a 'sabotage' probe into social media campaigns it says portray Georgia as unwelcoming to Russians.

media.caption: Russian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Maria Zakharova

events.confidenceReason: Direct quote from a Russian MFA briefing; underlying 'incidents' are not independently detailed.

events.title: Seven UN Security Council Members Condemn Russia's Occupation on 2008 War Anniversary
events.detail: Latvia, Denmark, France, Greece, the UK, Austria and Portugal issued a joint UN Security Council statement marking the 18th anniversary of the August 2008 Russo-Georgian war, condemning Russia's 'brutal invasion and continued illegal military presence' and citing unlawful detentions, restrictions on freedom of movement, discrimination against ethnic Georgians, and the killings of Giga Otkhozoria and Archil Tatunashvili. The statement called on Russia to implement the 2008 ceasefire agreement, withdraw its forces, and allow international human-rights monitors access to Abkhazia and South Ossetia.

media.caption: UN Security Council session marking the 18th anniversary of the 2008 Russo-Georgian war

events.confidenceReason: Official joint statement delivered at the UN Security Council.

events.title: 35th Saturday March Marks 633rd Consecutive Day of Protest
events.detail: Demonstrators marched from Avlabari metro station to the administration building under the slogan 'When the state serves Ivanishvili, cities and villages are devastated,' linking Georgia's mass emigration to Georgian Dream's policies. Core demands were unchanged: new parliamentary elections, release of political prisoners, and resumption of the EU accession path.

media.caption: Saturday march in Tbilisi, Aug 22, 2026 — the 633rd consecutive day of protest

events.title: Tbilisi Protesters Mark Ukraine's Independence Day with Solidarity March
events.detail: On the 635th consecutive day of anti-government protest, demonstrators gathered at the Ukrainian embassy in Tbilisi under the banner '#IndependenceInMyHeart' and marched to the Taras Shevchenko monument wearing Ukrainian national colors. Police prevented marchers from carrying large flags on the roadway and forced protesters to fold a large Ukrainian flag at the monument. Former president Salome Zourabichvili addressed the crowd: 'Our struggle and their struggle are the same. Today, all our hopes are placed on Ukraine's struggle.' A Ukrainian embassy representative, Anatoly Khrystenko, also spoke. The march ended at Parliament and the Tbilisi City Council.

media.caption: Protesters at the Aug 24, 2026 Tbilisi march marking Ukraine's Independence Day

events.confidenceReason: Directly observed protest event reported with on-record quotes from named participants.

events.title: Jailed Ex-PM Garibashvili Charged With New Bribery Count Carrying 11-15 Years
events.detail: Prosecutors personally presented Irakli Garibashvili with a new corruption charge alleging he took GEL 750,000 in cash from then-Defense Minister Juansher Burchuladze as his share of an inflated 2021-2024 Defense Ministry procurement scheme, in which equipment worth GEL 11.5 million was billed at GEL 18.5 million via three non-competitive classified contracts tied to businessman Zurab Tukvadze's Gori Military Hospital tender. The charge — taking a particularly large bribe as part of a group while holding political office — carries 11 to 15 years and comes days after Garibashvili's first public break with Ivanishvili, accusing the government of pressuring him into an earlier guilty plea. His lawyers say he denies guilt and will contest the case; his family calls it retaliation for speaking out.

media.caption: Former PM Irakli Garibashvili, charged Aug 24, 2026 with a new bribery count carrying 11-15 years

events.confidenceReason: Charge is a prosecutorial allegation, not yet adjudicated; Garibashvili denies guilt and his family calls the timing retaliatory given his recent public break with Ivanishvili.

events.title: Four Candidates Registered for Occupied Tskhinvali's Sept 18 'Presidential Vote'
events.detail: The de facto Central Election Commission in Russian-occupied Tskhinvali registered four candidates for the September 18, 2026 snap 'presidential' vote, called after Moscow-aligned incumbent Alan Gagloev resigned in June to become a Kremlin adviser: acting de facto leader Marat Kambolov (a North Ossetian-born former Russian official backed by Vladimir Putin and endorsed by three of the four parliamentary parties), Kazbeg Kodoev, Zurab Kokoev of the 'Unity' party, and Murat Valiev of 'Patriots of Alania.' A fifth applicant, Khokh Chochiev, was rejected over insufficient signatures and a failed state-language test. Georgia does not recognize the vote or South Ossetia's occupation authorities.

media.caption: Candidates in the running for Tskhinvali's Sept 18, 2026 de facto 'presidential' vote

events.confidenceReason: Confirmed by the de facto Tskhinvali election commission's own registration action, reported by independent Georgian and Russian-region outlets; Georgia does not recognize the process's legitimacy.

events.title: Eight Ivanishvili-Linked Companies Moved From Luxembourg Entity to His Wife's Name
events.detail: Eight companies previously held through the Georgian Co-Investment Fund's Luxembourg entity, GCF Luxembourg — including Galleria Holding (owner of Galleria Tbilisi mall), Axis Towers Holding, Mtkvari Holding, GreenHouse Holding, Agro Holding, Resort Holding, Lentekhi Holding and MV Holding — were registered directly in the name of Ekaterine Khvedelidze, wife of Georgian Dream founder Bidzina Ivanishvili, under a sale agreement signed August 24 as GCF Luxembourg entered liquidation. Khvedelidze was already the ultimate beneficial owner via GCF Luxembourg and its Cayman Islands parent, GCF LP. Analysts, including Center for Civic Participation head Irakli Abesadze, called it 'Ivanishvili's flight from offshore,' with Transparency International Georgia noting the move could shield the roughly 95 Ivanishvili-linked companies registered in British-jurisdiction territories from a possible future UK sanctions package.

media.caption: Eight Co-Investment Fund businesses registered in Ekaterine Khvedelidze's name, Aug 24, 2026

events.confidenceReason: Based on corporate registry documents and investigative reporting (RFE/RL), not an official government or Ivanishvili-camp statement.

events.title: Jailed Garibashvili Announces Boycott of Court Hearings, Calls Case a 'Political Masquerade'
events.detail: Days after being charged Aug 24 with a new bribery count carrying 11-15 years, imprisoned former PM Irakli Garibashvili skipped his Aug 25 hearing and released a prison letter declaring he saw no point in attending proceedings he called a 'disgraceful political masquerade,' saying he knew 'what and how the system controls the political process.' In an Aug 26 follow-up statement he said, 'I will no longer participate in your show! Nor am I interested in what you will make any prisoner/hostage write,' adding he would be represented solely by his lawyers while communicating with the public directly.

media.caption: Jailed former PM Irakli Garibashvili, who says he will boycott further court hearings

events.confidenceReason: Based on Garibashvili's own prison letter and public statement, reported by multiple Georgian outlets.

events.title: Georgian Dream Power Broker Mamuka Mdinaradze Resigns as Minister, Quits Politics
events.detail: Mamuka Mdinaradze — a decade-long Georgian Dream heavyweight who served as parliamentary faction chairman, majority leader and deputy speaker before becoming Minister of Regional Development, and a former State Security Service chief — abruptly resigned his ministerial post and announced he was quitting politics entirely, three days after jailed former PM Irakli Garibashvili's new bribery charges and his public break with party founder Bidzina Ivanishvili. Mdinaradze said the decision was his own after 'ten years of complete immersion in politics,' citing the psychological toll, while PM Irakli Kobakhidze said he and Ivanishvili had initially tried to talk him out of it. Opposition figures speculated he could face the same fate as Garibashvili; analyst Gia Khukhashvili quipped that 'a cabinet of ministers can be formed in prison.'

media.caption: Mamuka Mdinaradze announcing his resignation from politics, Aug 27, 2026

events.confidenceReason: Confirmed via Mdinaradze's own resignation announcement, reported by both Georgian and regional outlets.

events.title: Kavelashvili Pardons 226 Prisoners Including Nine Protest-Related Detainees
events.detail: President Mikheil Kavelashvili pardoned 226 people — 217 serving custodial sentences, six non-custodial, and three with records expunged — to mark the Orthodox feast of Mariamoba, in his first known clemency for a protest-related prisoner since the movement began. Among those released was Fridon Bubuteishvili, sentenced to five years for damaging Parliament's gate and injuring a firefighter during the spring 2024 anti-foreign-agents-law protests, who had applied for clemency roughly four months earlier. Eight other protest-related detainees — including participants in the Nov-Dec 2024 demonstrations and the Oct 4, 2025 'peaceful revolution' case, and Russian citizen Denis Kulanin, who faces possible deportation — were also among the 226. The Presidential Administration said the move reflected 'the principles of humanism and the national interest'; most individual names were not disclosed.

media.caption: President Kavelashvili's Aug 27, 2026 pardon list included nine protest-related detainees

events.confidenceReason: Confirmed by the Presidential Administration's own pardon decree, reported across multiple Georgian and regional outlets.

events.title: New German Ambassador Voss Assumes Office Amid Ties 'Marked by Tensions'
events.detail: Barbara Voss assumed office as Germany's ambassador-designate to Georgia, succeeding Peter Fischer, whose tenure was marked by repeated disputes with Georgian Dream after he criticized the party's anti-democratic actions — prompting Berlin to recall him for consultations in 2025 following months of Georgian officials 'agitating' against Germany, the EU and the ambassador himself. Voss said 'the existing tensions are weighing on Germany's and the European Union's relations with Georgia,' but that 'Germany's active support for the country's democratic and pro-European course remains unwaveringly strong.' The strain also delayed the reverse appointment: Georgia's ambassador to Berlin, Alexander Kartozia, did not present his credentials to German President Steinmeier until July 23, 2026 — nearly ten months after his appointment.

media.caption: German Ambassador Barbara Voss assumes office in Tbilisi, Aug 27, 2026

events.confidenceReason: Based on the ambassador's own on-record statement and diplomatic protocol records.

events.title: Protests Reach 638th Consecutive Day; 69-Year-Old Demonstrator Jailed 15 Days
events.detail: Demonstrations outside Parliament and the Tbilisi City Council continued into their 638th consecutive day, with protesters again demanding a return to the Euro-Atlantic course, the release of political prisoners, and free and fair elections, carrying signs reading 'Russia is an occupier' and 'Bidzina, you should also leave.' On day 637 (Aug 26), 69-year-old protest regular Shota Odishvili was arrested and given 15 days' administrative detention for insulting police officers.

media.caption: Tbilisi protesters near Parliament on the movement's 638th consecutive day

events.confidenceReason: Reported by independent regional monitor Kavkaz Uzel, consistent with the tracker's established daily-protest-count pattern.

events.title: Pardoned Teen Protester Saba Jikia Rejoins Tbilisi Demonstrations on Day 642
events.detail: Saba Jikia, sentenced to four and a half years in prison for allegedly kicking a police officer during the November 2024 demonstrations and long treated as a symbol of the crackdown on young protesters, rejoined the daily rally outside Parliament and Tbilisi City Hall days after President Kavelashvili's Aug 27 Mariamoba pardon of 226 prisoners, including nine protest-related detainees. His return on the movement's 642nd consecutive day was celebrated by fellow demonstrators as a rare visible win after nearly two years of continuous, largely fruitless daily protest.

media.caption: Protesters welcome pardoned activist Saba Jikia back to the Tbilisi rally on day 642

events.confidenceReason: Confirmed by direct on-the-ground reporting from Caucasian Knot and cross-referenced against Georgia Today's coverage of the underlying Aug 27 pardon.

events.title: Garibashvili's Fifth Prison Letter Questions 'Unanswered' Deaths Under Kobakhidze-Mdinaradze Rule
events.detail: In a fifth public letter from prison, jailed ex-PM Irakli Garibashvili said Mamuka Mdinaradze's Aug 27 resignation from politics could not erase the 'irreparable damage' he says Mdinaradze and PM Irakli Kobakhidze caused the country and Georgian Dream. He demanded answers over what he called unresolved suicides during the 'Kobakhidze-Mdinaradze rule,' singling out the case of rights defender Lazare Jorbenadze, who died shortly after a February 2026 interview criticizing Kobakhidze over alleged land concessions to Azerbaijan: 'The following question must be answered: what was the real reason for the death of rights defender Lazare Jorbenadze?' Conservative Georgian outlets had previously questioned the official suicide finding in Jorbenadze's death.

media.caption: Jailed ex-PM Irakli Garibashvili's fifth prison letter renewed questions over deaths under Kobakhidze-Mdinaradze rule

events.confidenceReason: The letter's contents and Garibashvili's allegations are independently reported by Civil.ge and Georgia Today, but the underlying claim about the cause of Jorbenadze's death remains an unverified allegation, not an established fact.

events.title: Pardoned Russian Activist Denis Kulanin Blocked From Leaving Georgia, Faces Deportation to Russia
events.detail: Denis Kulanin, a Russian national and former Navalny campaign volunteer pardoned Aug 27 alongside eight Georgian protest-related detainees, declared a dry hunger strike on Aug 29 over fears his passport was being withheld, ending it Aug 30 after his lawyer showed him the document. Supporters bought him a Sep 1 flight to Yerevan under a Tbilisi City Court order authorizing departure to a third country, but Georgia's Interior Ministry migration department blocked his exit and instead petitioned the court to expel him to Russia, where he faces prosecution over his public opposition to the invasion of Ukraine and support for Alexei Navalny. On the protest movement's 643rd consecutive day, demonstrators rallied in solidarity demanding he be allowed to leave for a safe third country. Amnesty International's Denis Krivosheev said Georgia is bound by the principle of non-refoulement and warned Kulanin faces a 'genuine risk of serious human rights violations' if returned to Russia.

media.caption: Amnesty International warns pardoned Russian activist Denis Kulanin faces forcible deportation to Russia

events.confidenceReason: Corroborated by Meduza and Caucasian Knot reporting citing Kulanin's lawyer and case manager, plus an on-the-record Amnesty International statement; Georgian authorities have not disputed the underlying facts.
